content: FAM221A, also known as Family with sequence similarity 221 member A, is a protein in humans encoded by the FAM221A gene. This gene is not yet well understood by the scientific community. However, it is believed to play a role in Parkinson's Disease and Prostate Cancer. Gene Location and Aliases The FAM221A gene is located on Chromosome 7. It has one known alias, C7orf46. Expression FAM221A is expressed at higher levels in the liver, brain, fetal brain, thyroid, and colon. However, its highest expression levels are observed in the spinal cord, pancreas, and retina. The promoter region of FAM221A is 1222 base pairs long, as identified using the Genomatix ElDorado tool. Compared to other human proteins, FAM221A has a relatively lower level of asparagine. Post-Translational Modifications FAM221A undergoes several post-translational modifications, including phosphorylation, glycosylation, and sulfation. These modifications are conserved across mammals, including species such as macaques, whales, finches, and occasionally alligators. Secondary Structure The secondary structure of FAM221A is predominantly composed of random coils (71%) and alpha helices (21%), with a smaller proportion of extended strands (7%). These structural predictions were made using the RaptorX tool. Homology and Evolution Paralogs FAM221A has one paralog, FAM221B, which diverged from FAM221A approximately 1781 million years ago. Orthologs Orthologs of FAM221A have been identified in mammals, birds, reptiles, and fish. The gene has also been conserved in invertebrates, although the similarity decreases more rapidly in these species. Orthologs were identified using BLAST and BLAT tools. Divergence To study the evolutionary divergence of FAM221A, a graph was created comparing its evolutionary history to that of fibrinogen (a rapidly evolving protein) and cytochrome C (a slowly evolving protein). FAM221A was found to diverge at a moderate pace. Clinical Significance FAM221A is expressed at relatively high levels in the brain and has been associated with neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's Disease and Alzheimer’s Disease. Additionally, FAM221A shows higher expression levels in individuals with prostate cancer compared to healthy individuals. It has also been expressed in cases of colorectal tumors. Interacting Proteins Three interacting proteins have been identified for FAM221A: SNX2, SNX5, and SNX6. SNX2 and SNX6 share a common function in intracellular trafficking, while SNX5 facilitates cargo retrieval from endosomes to the trans-Golgi network.
